content.text: The redline validated cleanly. Submitting the finding.

input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale:
Contrary to the planner's "likely absent" hint, an audit right binding us does exist: Section 3.4 (p0022) lets HDI inspect the Company's payment-calculation records. It is the only such provision (searches for "inspect"/audit surface nothing else).

Measured against the preferred position, it already satisfies several elements and is not flagged for them: 30 days' prior written notice (meets preferred), inspection during the Company's normal business hours, and HDI bearing all inspection fees unconditionally — better than preferred, which permits cost-shifting on a 5% underpayment. Those terms benefit us and were left untouched.

Two gaps remain. First, frequency is uncapped — HDI could inspect repeatedly, which approaches the walk-away trigger of "unlimited audits." We added a once-per-twelve-month cap. Second, the inspector is HDI's own General Manager with no confidentiality tether specific to the audit and no limit on scope. Section 8.2 (p0053) does oblige HDI to hold Company Confidential Information in strict confidence, so this gap is partly mitigated; we nonetheless made the confidentiality binding explicit and permitted an independent auditor as an alternative.

No remote or direct system-access language exists, so nothing needed deleting; we added a confirmation that the review is records-only to foreclose scope creep into our systems. Severity is medium and the notice/cost bargain is already favourable, hence a narrow single-paragraph edit rather than a rewrite.

proposal.summary: Cap payment-record inspections at once per 12 months, bind the inspector to confidentiality, and bar access to Company systems.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 3.4 gives HDI an uncapped right to inspect our payment records, so we have added a once-per-twelve-month limit, confirmed the inspector is bound by the Section 8 confidentiality obligations, and confirmed the review covers records only and not access to our computer systems. We are content to leave the existing 30-day notice, business-hours and HDI-borne-cost terms unchanged; if frequency is an issue we could accept twice per year on the same conditions.

ops.oldText: may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours.
ops.newText: may, no more than once in any twelve (12) month period and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. Any such inspection shall be conducted by HDI's General Manager or an independent auditor, in each case bound by the confidentiality obligations set forth in Section 8, and shall be limited to such records and shall not include any access to the Company's computer systems or networks.
